## raw data cleaning

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# India air quality - clean raw CPCB daily bulletins & plot pollutant seasonality
# Raw source: UrbanEmissions.info compilation of CPCB National AQI bulletins
#             (CC BY 4.0). Attribute CPCB + UrbanEmissions.info.
#
# Every add-on-package function is called as pkg:: so no library() is needed and
# masking can't happen. Base R functions are left unprefixed. Required packages
# (must be INSTALLED): tidyverse, and legendry for the season brackets.
#   install.packages(c("tidyverse", "legendry"))   # run once if needed
# legendry needs R >= 4.1 and ggplot2 >= 3.5.2.
# =============================================================================

# The pipe is an operator and cannot be written pkg::%>% inline, so import it once:
`%>%` <- magrittr::`%>%`

## the raw data used from the link below (UrbanEmissions.info) here spans from 2015 to 2025 at the moment when this project was written
raw_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/urbanemissionsinfo/AQI_bulletins/main/data/Processed/AllIndiaBulletinsMaster2025_openrefined.csv"

# ---- 1. Read raw ------------------------------------------------------------
# Raw columns: date, city, no_stations, aqi_category, aqi, prominent_pollutant
raw <- readr::read_csv(raw_url, show_col_types = FALSE)

# ---- 2. Helper: normalize a pollutant token --------------------------------
norm_pollutant <- function(x) {
  x <- stringr::str_to_upper(stringr::str_trim(x))
  dplyr::recode(x,
    "OZONE" = "O3", "O3" = "O3",
    "PM2.5" = "PM2.5", "PM10" = "PM10",
    "NO2" = "NO2", "SO2" = "SO2", "CO" = "CO", "NH3" = "NH3",
    .default = stringr::str_to_title(x)
  )
}

# ---- 3. Clean ---------------------------------------------------------------
clean <- raw %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    n_stations    = no_stations,
    pollutant_raw = prominent_pollutant
  ) %>%                                              # city, aqi already named
  dplyr::mutate(
    date       = lubridate::as_date(date),
    aqi        = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(aqi)),
    n_stations = dplyr::na_if(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(n_stations)), 0)  # 0 = not reported
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(date), !is.na(city), !is.na(aqi)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    aqi_category = cut(
      aqi,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, Inf),
      labels = c("Good", "Satisfactory", "Moderate", "Poor", "Very Poor", "Severe")
    ),
    tokens = stringr::str_split(stringr::str_replace_all(pollutant_raw, ";", ","), ","),
    tokens = purrr::map(tokens, function(t) {
      t <- norm_pollutant(t)
      unique(t[t != "" & !is.na(t)])
    }),
    pollutant_primary = purrr::map_chr(tokens, function(t) if (length(t)) t[[1]] else NA_character_),
    pollutant_set     = purrr::map_chr(tokens, function(t) if (length(t)) paste(sort(t), collapse = " + ") else NA_character_),
    n_prominent       = lengths(tokens),
    drv_pm25 = purrr::map_int(tokens, function(t) as.integer("PM2.5" %in% t)),
    drv_pm10 = purrr::map_int(tokens, function(t) as.integer("PM10"  %in% t)),
    drv_o3   = purrr::map_int(tokens, function(t) as.integer("O3"    %in% t)),
    drv_no2  = purrr::map_int(tokens, function(t) as.integer("NO2"   %in% t)),
    drv_so2  = purrr::map_int(tokens, function(t) as.integer("SO2"   %in% t)),
    drv_co   = purrr::map_int(tokens, function(t) as.integer("CO"    %in% t)),
    drv_nh3  = purrr::map_int(tokens, function(t) as.integer("NH3"   %in% t)),
    year        = lubridate::year(date),
    month       = lubridate::month(date),
    month_name  = lubridate::month(date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
    day_of_week = lubridate::wday(date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
    is_weekend  = as.integer(lubridate::wday(date) %in% c(1, 7)),  # 1 = Sun, 7 = Sat
    season = dplyr::case_when(
      month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
      month %in% 3:6         ~ "Summer",
      month %in% 7:9         ~ "Monsoon",
      TRUE                   ~ "Post-monsoon"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    date, city, year, month, month_name, season, day_of_week, is_weekend,
    aqi, aqi_category, pollutant_primary, pollutant_set, n_prominent,
    drv_pm25, drv_pm10, drv_o3, drv_no2, drv_so2, drv_co, drv_nh3, n_stations
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(city, date)

# readr::write_csv(clean, "india_aqi_daily_2015_2025.csv")

# ---- 4. Aggregate: prominent-pollutant share by month (FRACTIONAL CREDIT) ----
main_poll <- c("PM2.5", "PM10", "O3", "CO", "NO2", "SO2", "NH3")

monthly_share <- clean %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_prominent >= 1) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    month, month_name,
    PM2.5 = drv_pm25, PM10 = drv_pm10, O3 = drv_o3,
    CO = drv_co, NO2 = drv_no2, SO2 = drv_so2, NH3 = drv_nh3,
    w = 1 / n_prominent
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(PM2.5, PM10, O3, CO, NO2, SO2, NH3),
    names_to = "pollutant", values_to = "flag"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(flag == 1) %>%
  dplyr::count(month, month_name, pollutant, wt = w, name = "days") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(month_name) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(share = 100 * days / sum(days)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pollutant = factor(pollutant, levels = rev(main_poll)))

# Season grouping. Winter (Dec, Jan, Feb) is only contiguous if the year starts
# in December, so we relabel the x-axis Dec -> Nov; then all four seasons are
# adjacent blocks. xpos is the Dec-first position (Dec = 1 ... Nov = 12).
season_levels <- c("Winter", "Summer", "Monsoon", "Post-monsoon")
decfirst_lab  <- c("Dec", "Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May",
                   "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov")

add_season <- function(df) {
  df %>% dplyr::mutate(
    season = factor(dplyr::case_when(
      month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
      month %in% 3:6         ~ "Summer",
      month %in% 7:9         ~ "Monsoon",
      TRUE                   ~ "Post-monsoon"
    ), levels = season_levels),
    xpos = (month %% 12) + 1                       # Dec=1, Jan=2, ..., Nov=12
  )
}

monthly_share <- monthly_share %>%
  add_season() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month_name = factor(as.character(month_name), levels = decfirst_lab))

# ---- 4b. EVERY NUMBER QUOTED IN THE BLOG (run this, paste the console output) -
# Each print below is tagged [B#] with the sentence it backs in the post.

cat("\n[B1] Dataset shape -----------------------------------------------------\n")
cat("rows (city-days):      ", nrow(clean), "\n")
cat("distinct cities:       ", dplyr::n_distinct(clean$city), "\n")
cat("date range:            ", format(min(clean$date)), "to", format(max(clean$date)), "\n")
cat("AQI value range:       ", min(clean$aqi), "to", max(clean$aqi), "\n")

cat("\n[B2] Share of city-days that list MORE THAN ONE prominent pollutant ------\n")
multi_pct <- clean %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_prominent >= 1) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(multi_pct = round(100 * mean(n_prominent > 1), 1))
print(multi_pct)

cat("\n[B3] Overall share of city-days each pollutant is PROMINENT --------------\n")
# Fractional credit split across days that list several. NOT month-wise.
overall_share <- clean %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_prominent >= 1) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    PM2.5 = drv_pm25, PM10 = drv_pm10, O3 = drv_o3,
    CO = drv_co, NO2 = drv_no2, SO2 = drv_so2, NH3 = drv_nh3,
    w = 1 / n_prominent
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-w, names_to = "pollutant", values_to = "flag") %>%
  dplyr::filter(flag == 1) %>%
  dplyr::count(pollutant, wt = w, name = "credit") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(share_pct = round(100 * credit / sum(credit), 1)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(share_pct))
print(overall_share)

cat("\n[B4] Share by season (top pollutant per season, and O3/CO peaks) ---------\n")
season_share <- clean %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_prominent >= 1) %>%
  add_season() %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    season,
    PM2.5 = drv_pm25, PM10 = drv_pm10, O3 = drv_o3,
    CO = drv_co, NO2 = drv_no2, SO2 = drv_so2, NH3 = drv_nh3,
    w = 1 / n_prominent
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(-season, -w), names_to = "pollutant", values_to = "flag") %>%
  dplyr::filter(flag == 1) %>%
  dplyr::count(season, pollutant, wt = w, name = "credit") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(season) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(share_pct = round(100 * credit / sum(credit), 1)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::arrange(season, dplyr::desc(share_pct))
print(season_share, n = Inf)

cat("\n[B5] Check: each month's shares sum to 100% (plotted summary table) -------\n")
month_totals <- monthly_share %>%
  dplyr::group_by(month_name) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(total_pct = round(sum(share), 1), .groups = "drop")
print(month_totals, n = Inf)

cat("\n[B6] Coverage grows over time: cities & mean stations reporting per year --\n")
coverage_by_year <- clean %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    cities        = dplyr::n_distinct(city),
    mean_stations = round(mean(n_stations, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(coverage_by_year, n = Inf)

cat("\n[B7] Month-by-month: peak month for each pollutant (the plotted summary) --\n")
# For each pollutant, the calendar month where its prominent-share is highest.
monthly_peaks <- monthly_share %>%
  dplyr::group_by(pollutant) %>%
  dplyr::slice_max(share, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::transmute(pollutant, peak_month = as.character(month_name),
                   peak_share_pct = round(share, 1)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(peak_share_pct))
print(monthly_peaks)

# ---- 5. Shared palette, theme & a per-plot label builder --------------------
pal <- c(
  "PM2.5" = "#4e79a7", "PM10" = "#f28e2b", "O3" = "#59a14f",
  "CO"    = "#edc948", "NO2"  = "#e15759", "SO2" = "#b07aa1",
  "NH3"   = "#76b7b2"
)

descriptor <- "Share of city-days by prominent pollutant |  297 cities  |  2015-2025 (pooled)"

# labs_for(): same title/descriptor/caption for every plot, but a plot-specific
# interpretation paragraph wrapped and placed under the subtitle.
labs_for <- function(interp) {
  ggplot2::labs(
    title    = "Which pollutant drives India's air, month by month",
    subtitle = paste0(descriptor, "\n\n", stringr::str_wrap(interp, width = 96)),
    x = NULL, y = "Share of city-days (across 15 years)",
    caption  = "Graphic: github.com/AarshBatra/biteSizedAQ | Data Credit: CPCB daily AQI bulletins, compiled by UrbanEmissions.info"
  )
}

interp_bar <- paste(
  "Each bar is one calendar month, with all eleven years (2015-2025) pooled together. Each bar's coloured",
  "slices show how often (across 15 years) each pollutant topped the air that month: the taller a slice, the more days",
  "that pollutant led that month. Blue (PM2.5) fills the winter bars - so for more than 50% of January days PM2.5 was the most prominent pollutant, orange (PM10 dust) takes over through",
  "summer, and green (ozone) and yellow (CO) grow in the summer and monsoon months. Every",
  "bar adds up to 100%."
)

interp_area <- paste(
  "Each coloured band shows how often a pollutant topped the air, month by month, with every calendar",
  "month pooling all eleven years (2015-2025). Follow one band across the year: blue (PM2.5) is widest",
  "in winter months - so for more than 50% of January days PM2.5 was the most prominent pollutant, orange (PM10 dust) runs through summer months, and green (ozone) and yellow (CO)",
  "swell in the summer and monsoon months. Each month adds up to 100%."
)

shared_theme <- ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x          = ggplot2::element_text(size = 16, margin = margin(t = 6)),
     axis.text.y          = ggplot2::element_text(size = 16, margin = margin(r = 6)),
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 17),
    panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    plot.title         = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 20),
    # gap between the interpretation paragraph and the legend below it:
    plot.subtitle      = ggplot2::element_text(lineheight = 1.15,
                                               margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 16), size = 18.5),
    legend.position    = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    # legend in a box:
    legend.background  = ggplot2::element_rect(colour = "grey70", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.margin      = ggplot2::margin(6, 10, 6, 10),
    legend.box.margin  = ggplot2::margin(t = 2, b = 10),
    legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 16),
    # gap between the plotting area and the caption:
    plot.caption       = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "grey40",
                                               margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 18), size = 13),
    plot.margin        = ggplot2::margin(12, 18, 12, 12)
  )

# Season brackets on a SINGLE continuous axis (no faceting). legendry draws the
# normal month ticks, then a bracket + season name beneath each month range.
# start/end are Dec-first positions: Winter 1-3, Summer 4-7, Monsoon 8-10, Post 11-12.
season_key <- legendry::key_range_manual(
  start = c(1, 4, 8, 11),
  end   = c(3, 7, 10, 12),
  name  = season_levels
)
season_guide <- legendry::guide_axis_nested(key = season_key)

# ---- 6. Plot p: 100% stacked BAR --------------------------------------------
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(monthly_share,
                     ggplot2::aes(x = xpos, y = share, fill = pollutant)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.82, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = pal, breaks = main_poll, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = decfirst_lab,
                              expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = 0.6),
                              guide = season_guide) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(0), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs_for(interp_bar) + shared_theme

print(p)
ggplot2::ggsave("./30.bite.sized.vis.6.india.aq.pollutants.season.trends/images/india_pollutant_by_month_bar.png", p, width = 15.5, height = 12.5, dpi = 520)

# ---- 7. Plot area_share: 100% stacked AREA ----------------------------------
# Area needs a value at every month x pollutant cell, so complete the grid with 0s.
area_df <- monthly_share %>%
  tidyr::complete(month, pollutant, fill = list(share = 0)) %>%
  add_season()                                     # recompute season/xpos after complete

area_share <- ggplot2::ggplot(area_df,
                              ggplot2::aes(x = xpos, y = share, fill = pollutant)) +
  ggplot2::geom_area(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = pal, breaks = main_poll, name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:12, labels = decfirst_lab,
                              expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = 0.02),
                              guide = season_guide) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(0), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs_for(interp_area) + shared_theme

print(area_share)
ggplot2::ggsave("./30.bite.sized.vis.6.india.aq.pollutants.season.trends/images/india_pollutant_by_month_area.png", area_share, width = 15.5, height = 12.5, dpi = 520)
```
